basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 21.' and it opens '(Vers. 21.) Et profectus est Israel: et extendit tabernaculum suum trans turrim Ader.'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 21.) Et profectus est Israel: et extendit tabernaculum suum trans turrim Ader. Hunc locum Hebraei esse volunt, ubi postea templum aedificatum est: et turrim Ader, turrim gregis significare, hoc est, congregationis et coetus: quod et Michaeas Propheta testatur, dicens: Et tu turris gregis nebulosa, filia Sion (Mich. IV, 8), et caetera: illoque tempore Jacob trans locum, ubi postea templum aedificatum est, habuisse tentoria. Sed si sequamur ordinem viae, pastorum juxta Bethleem locus est, ubi vel Angelorum rex in ortu Domini cecinit: vel Jacob pecora sua pavit, loco nomen imponens: vel quod verius est, quodam vaticinio futurum jam tunc mysterium monstrabatur,
